- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly above recent mean.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture momentum — align forecast with 3–5 day moving average of true price.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates upward momentum in bullish sentiment periods — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.67 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment turns sharply bullish after a downtrend, model often lags — forecast should be adjusted 1–2 days ahead of true price to capture sentiment shift.
